**Finding repaired and submitted: deviation (was compliant).**

What changed and why:

- **Accepted the mis-classification.** §1.4 grants access and use rights to "the Company" only — no affiliates, no contractors, no written-notice mechanic — so a material term of the fallback (affiliate coverage at minimum on notice) is unmet.
- **Corrected the flawed premise.** My prior rationale asserted there was "no restriction preventing" affiliate/contractor use; §10.3's "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement" affirmatively excludes them and leaves no path to add them — the rule's walk-away trigger.
- **Downgraded the §10.3 successor argument.** It is a standard binding-effect/successors-and-assigns clause: it confirms the Agreement inures to successors but grants no affirmative M&A transfer right, so it only weakly supports the second fallback limb and cannot cure the affiliate gap.
- **Redline validated (ok:true), preferred level, precedent `seed-license`:** extends the §1.4 access/use rights to our affiliates (with a control-based definition, as "Affiliate" is undefined in this document) and contractors acting on our behalf plus transfer to an M&A successor; and carves those parties out of the §10.3 "no other person" limitation. The [Playbook] comment offers the affiliates-on-written-notice fallback.
- No revocability deletion was needed (the grant is not revocable at HDI's discretion), and term/termination mechanics remain with the term rule to avoid double-flagging.
